If $\mathcal N$ has genus one, exactly one block has a
genus-one neighborhood. The merged walk is the only
boundary walk meeting both blocks. In the other block
it passes through $s_3$ or $t_3$ and only one vertex
of $A$, so no boundary walk meets all of $A$.
Every complementary region is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, a contradiction.

If $\mathcal N$ has genus zero, the five boundary walks meet
$A$, for some $i,j\in\{1,2\}$, in
\[
\{s_i,t_j\},\qquad
\{s_1,s_2\},\qquad
\{s_{3-i}\},\qquad
\{t_1,t_2\},\qquad
\{t_{3-j}\}.
\]
No one walk meets all of $A$, and the only pair doing
so consists of the walks through $\{s_1,s_2\}$ and
$\{t_1,t_2\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement},
the drawing of $B$ away from $A$ therefore lies in
the annular face bounded by these walks. Each
attachment appears once on its boundary walk, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} makes $B+E$ planar.

By Kuratowski's theorem, $H_1+E$ contains a $K_{3,3}$
subdivision. Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision},
with attachment set $A$ and this set $E$, gives
an allowed minor $H_1'$ of $H_1$ with $H_1'+E$ nonplanar.
The allowed operations preserve the hypotheses on
$B$, so $H_0\cup H_1'$ is nontoroidal by the implication
just proved. Any nontrivial sequence gives a proper
minor of $G$, so minimality forces $H_1'=H_1$.
Thus $G$ itself occurs among the candidates of
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}.
The exclusions discard every such candidate~\supp{E1}, a contradiction.
